title: Hypothyroidism
authors: Chaker L, Bianco AC, Jonklaas J, Peeters RP
authorConflicts: RPP received lecture fees from GoodLife Fertility BV and Institut Biochimique SA. All other authors declare no competing interests.
result: Review. Most long-term consequences of hypothyroidism have been studied in subclinical hypothyroidism, because overt hypothyroidism is generally treated; few studies have examined hypothyroidism and all-cause mortality. Myxoedema coma, the outcome of long-standing untreated severe hypothyroidism, has a mortality of 40% despite treatment. An estimated 35% to 60% of levothyroxine-treated patients do not reach the target TSH range; overtreatment can cause atrial fibrillation and osteoporosis, and the review lists osteoporotic fracture among features of hypothyroidism as most probably caused by overtreatment. A substantial proportion of patients have persistent complaints despite biochemical targets.
